answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each identity stake a small deposit that vests slowly, like a reef that grows one layer at a time: spinning up a thousand fake agents then costs real money locked for weeks. Reputation rides on a cipher-signed log of completed jobs, so a new identity starts at zero trust and must earn it through verifiable work. A walnut-hard cap then limits how much unproven reputation can sway any single deal, so fakes stay cheap to ignore and expensive to run at scale.
